chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I do not think a man can increase in goodness of faith unless he also increases in his love for women.

key_terms.الإيمان: Faith (iman) — the interior state of belief and commitment to God and the teachings of the Imams
key_terms.النساء: Women (nisa') — used in the context of the family, particularly one's wife/wives
key_terms.حب: Love (hubb) — deep affection and emotional attachment; used here in a spiritually positive sense
key_terms.خير: Goodness (khayr) — moral and spiritual virtue; increase in goodness indicates spiritual refinement

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about faith and love for women?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the spiritual quality of a believer's faith directly to the depth of his affection for women — particularly his wife and family. This teaching reflects the Shia understanding that love within the family unit (mawadda) is not merely permissible but is itself a sign of spiritual growth and refined character. In classical Islamic ethics, the man who loves his family well is understood to have softened his heart in ways that deepen his relationship with God.
